items.title: US embassy accuses Canada of election meddling ahead of midterms
items.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney dismissed the claim, noting that it was the that US initiated trade actions against Canada.
items.content:
The US Embassy in Ottawa has accused Canadian officials of election meddling ahead of the November midterms.

The embassy said Canadian leaders have brushed off concerns over "potential interference", and that ministers and premiers "openly describe plans to influence American politics in official documents and public appearances".

Canadian leaders, including Prime Minister Mark Carney, have dismissed the claims. Relations between the North American neighbours have hardened during second Trump administration.

The midterms will determine which political party controls both branches of the US Congress, which could have a significant impact on the rest of Donald Trump's presidency.

The fact sheet released by the US Embassy on Wednesday alleges the Canadian government "brushes off concerns about potential interference in U.S. elections, even as its ministers and premiers openly describe plans to influence American politics in official documents and public appearances".

It cites comments and actions, like meetings with US Democrats and calling for retaliatory tariffs against the US.

For example, it says that when Industry Minister Mélanie Joly was asked what she expected regarding tariffs if Democrats were to win midterm elections, she responded, "That's exactly why I'm meeting so many governors and potential presidential candidates."

Ontario Premier Doug Ford pushed Canada's federal government, it states, to consider additional retaliatory tariffs on imports from "politically significant states to the current administration's base of support".

Asked on Wednesday about the allegations, Carney noted that it was the US that first initiated trade actions against Canada.

"We've responded to those to protect Canadian jobs, to protect Canadian companies and develop our economy," Carney said.

He said his government's response has been "in the interests of Canadian workers, Canadian families and the future of this economy".

Carney, who was announcing a nearly C$9bn ($6.2bn) aid package in response to US tariffs, was accompanied by both Joly and Ford.

Ford said that he has "no interest at all" in interfering in US elections.

"I'll tell you what the American people want. They want certainty, they want stability," Ford said, adding that he will focus on Ontario and Canada.

"The people of the United States will make that determination in the midterms," he said.

Last week, Minister Joly denied Canadian interference and said that Canadians "never accept that also being done to us in Canada", according to CBC.

She said that her recent visits to the US were "to attract investments" from American companies, which she plans to continue.

Washington and Ottawa have argued for months over tariffs and trade , which once flowed freely across their borders, and the effects of Canada's counter measures.

Earlier this month, US Ambassador to Canada Pete Hoekstra warned that US officials are "closely watching" Canada's politicians for signs of election interference.

Trump administration officials have also been accused of making inappropriate remarks about the separation referendum in the province of Alberta this week.

A petition calling for Hoekstra's removal from his post for "undermining the Canada-U.S. diplomatic relations" has received more than 280,000 signatures.

items.title: WorldTUI: I trained a 360M model to pretend to be a terminal
items.summary: Article URL: https://simedw.com/2026/10/21/world-model-terminal/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50190363 Points: 39 # Comments: 12
items.content:
TL;DR: I fine-tuned a 360M-parameter language model to act as a terminal. There's no shell or filesystem behind it: every keypress goes in, and the model predicts how the screen changes. It can create files, run vim and tmux, play snake, and usually remembers what you wrote a few commands later. The biggest wins were teaching it to repair its own mistakes and decoding screen rows in parallel. Try it in your browser (208 MB) and type pythoon to see that it's not a real shell.

The demo is designed for a desktop browser with WebGPU and a physical keyboard. Chrome or Edge is the best place to try it. It should work on a modern phone, but painfully slowly.

When I first saw Genie 3 last year, I started imagining a future where applications aren't written in code but learned. Instead of a game engine rendering the scene, a model predicts the next most likely frame from the user's inputs.

Naturally I wanted to train my own world model. But I don't have a massive GPU cluster or a pile of video data, so I scaled down my ambition: instead of a game world, a terminal.

A terminal turned out to be a good fit. It's just a grid of characters rather than pixels, and I can generate as much perfectly labelled training data as I want by running real shells. A pretrained language model also already has a pretty good idea of what ls or cat should print.

What I really wanted to know was whether it could maintain a consistent world, or just generate convincing terminal output.

The final model is based on Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B, fine-tuned on terminal sessions recorded from real programs running inside Docker. Jump to example videos

Standard LLMs take a prompt and then append tokens to the end, one at a time. That doesn't map well to a terminal. A single keypress can do something on its own, like esc in vim, and output doesn't always go to the bottom: clear wipes the screen and sends the cursor back to the top. So instead of predicting a stream of text, I need to predict changes to the screen.

I treat the terminal as a grid of characters, one per cell. 1 The model doesn't see the grid directly, but a sequence of tokens describing its contents and the changes made to it.

Every session starts with a snapshot: the screen size, its contents and where the cursor is.

The size is part of the input, not fixed at 32×96. In the demo, you can set the rows and columns when creating a custom starting screen.

This also lets me start partway through an application. Give it a bash prompt, vim buffer or a game of snake, and the model tries to continue from there. (It does better from bash.)

After that, each keypress goes in as the raw bytes a real terminal would send. Letters are themselves, Enter is \r , Escape is 0x1b and ← is ESC [ D and so on.

The model answers with which rows to rewrite and where the cursor ends up:

In words: on row 0, starting at column 17, write l , then move the cursor to row 0, column 18. The last 1 means the cursor is visible, since full-screen apps sometimes hide it.

Nothing gets cleared first. New characters are simply drawn over the old ones.

I didn't need new tokens for characters. Qwen already has tokens for all 256 byte values, which I reuse for characters, coordinates and other small numbers. So a coordinate like 17 takes one token, not two.

Time is an input too. If nothing is pressed, the model gets a WAIT token with a duration instead of a key, which is how snake keeps moving on its own.

When you reach the bottom of the terminal window and press enter, every line has to move up by one. I could just ask the model to output every row again in its new place, but that's around 3,000 tokens for a single keypress.

Each operation copies a row from the previous screen. In this example, the old row 1 becomes row 0, row 2 becomes row 1, and so on.

A scroll now costs three tokens per row instead of roughly 96.

The same trick covers clearing the screen, inserting and deleting lines in vim, and navigating man pages. You can also copy a row and then overwrite part of it.

Altogether, the model uses a tiny vocabulary of 333 tokens: 256 byte tokens, 64 row tokens and a handful of special operations. Decoding is grammar-constrained, so every prediction is a valid screen update.

That tiny vocabulary comes back later, when I squeeze the model into a browser.

I initially looked for existing datasets of terminal recordings, including asciinema, but couldn't find one with the precise keystroke-to-screen alignment I needed.

The basic idea was to generate believable terminal sessions by running real commands inside Docker containers, recording every keypress and the screen after each one.

The terminal size was mostly 32×96, with some 24×80 and 40×120, so the model doesn't overfit to one size.

I kept expanding the dataset as the model became more capable, and finally landed on 336k episodes, which corresponds to roughly 2B tokens. For comparison, the base model saw around 18T tokens during training.

I used Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B as the starting point. I needed a small model to get close to realtime performance. Being a coding model, it had also already seen plenty of CLI usage.

I started off by doing straightforward supervised fine-tuning: give a screen history and a keypress, predict the screen delta produced by the real terminal.

Ordinary typing was learned quickly: a letter appears, backspace removes it, the cursor moves.

In longer sessions, though, errors started to compound: a mistake in a filename propagated through the rest of the session.

To address this I took a page from DAgger, where a model learns from the states it visits rather than just the ideal demonstrations. 2

The delta takes the model's incorrect screen to the correct next screen. In essence, it learns to "repair" its own mistakes.

There's one important restriction: the model must have enough information to infer the correction. Any words introduced by a correction must have appeared on an earlier real screen or in the user's typing, not just in the model's own predictions.

For example, if the model misspells a filename that appeared earlier, I can teach it to fix that. But if it lists a filename it has never seen, I can't expect it to get it right.

Training on those examples would actually reward hallucinations, which I really don't need more of.

About a third of the sampled sessions produced useful correction examples. I repeated this in three rounds, each time collecting mistakes from the latest model.

Self-correction was one of the more effective training changes. Along with some additional training data, it improved PresetBench (defined below) from 24/47 to 38/47 at int4.

In total, training the model and its later refinements took roughly 75 GPU-hours on an RTX 4090.

I use three tests. ShellBench has 106 commands across 24 handwritten bash sessions, scored by exact output. PresetBench has 47 scripted cases drawn from failures I hit in the demo. Neither test appears in the training data.

The memory test has 32 worlds. Each writes two random values to two files, then reads them back in separate sessions. A world passes only if both readbacks are exact, giving 64 readbacks overall. The names and values never appear in training. 3

The biggest difference was memory: WorldTUI got 9/13 readbacks right, compared with 2/13 and 3/13 for the prompted models.

It's still far from a reliable filesystem. It handles familiar commands fairly well, but combining them in new ways can quickly break things. For example, after echo green >> colors , running cat colors often doesn't show the appended line.

For a while I stayed away from autoregressive models altogether. A full redraw is around 3,000 tokens, and generating those one at a time seemed hopeless for something that's supposed to feel like a terminal.

But they just performed so much better than the alternatives I tried, so I gave in. With one token at a time, typing felt fine at ~38 ms per key, but anything that redraws the whole screen ( vim test.txt , man , clear ) took up to 12 s on my RTX 4090, exactly as feared. Plenty of time to reconsider whether I needed the manual. And I wanted this to run on my Mac, in near real-time.

What I'd missed was that most rows in a frame don't depend on each other, so there's no reason to generate them one after another. I run one batch element per row. Each gets the same previous history (including KV cache) but generates only its own update.

That changes the decoding cost from the sum of all rows, up to 3,000 steps, to the length of the longest row, roughly 100 steps.

The cursor then becomes its own step at the end that can see the whole set of row updates.

This required a matching attention mask during training, but the speed improvement was worth it. Large-frame p95 latency dropped from 6.7 s to 0.87 s.

This might sound too good to be true, and it was. The issue is that since rows are independent, they can't coordinate, which led to vim opening on row 3 instead of row 0, or several rows adding food for snake at once.

Normally speculative decoding uses a small model to draft tokens and a larger model to verify them. Thanks to causal attention, several tokens can be verified in a single forward pass.

items.title: LLM agents play Pokemon showdown
items.summary: Article URL: https://olivergrabner.com/research/pokemon/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50190334 Points: 25 # Comments: 14
items.content:
The future is in LLM collaborations, and it is important to be able to understand how good agents are at working together, communicating and negotiating actions. Most multi-agent research is about workflows, where agents pass tasks down a pipeline ( Hong et al., 2024 ; Qian et al., 2024 ). To test this, I built a multi-agent environment on Pokémon Showdown's 2v2 format to evaluate these abilities.

Pokémon doubles is a game-theory environment without full information. The opponents' sets are hidden and damage is random, so winning takes real strategy: reading the other team, splitting targets and planning around your partner. Recent work like the PokéAgent Challenge ( Karten et al., 2026 ) benchmarks Pokémon battling, but each side is played by a single agent, and specialist RL agents still outplay general LLMs there. It doesn't test teammates who have to coordinate.

The goal is a controlled environment where I can measure how LLM agents coordinate, and that can later be used to train them with RL to encourage these collaborative behaviors.

The official Pokémon Showdown simulator, wrapped as a Gym-style environment. Four players each control one Pokémon from a team of three, two per side.

Each turn, an agent reads a plain-English summary of the battle and a numbered list of its legal moves. It can say a private message to its partner or choose a move, and once it chooses, its partner is told what it picked.

Free talk (keep talking until both have chosen), one message each, no talk, and one model controlling both Pokémon.

Qwen3.8-27B plays both teammates against a scripted max-damage bot. Battles are seeded and every team draw is played from both sides, so each talk mode faces exactly the same battles.

Talking helps. Teammates who could talk freely won 64% of their battles against the max-damage bot, while teammates who couldn't talk at all won 42%. Even a single message each (52%) beat no talk. One model controlling both Pokémon (54%) did better than no talk but worse than two agents talking freely, so I think the gain comes from the conversation itself, not just from one mind planning both moves.

Talking also costs. Free talk used 978k prompt tokens per battle, 3.8x the 259k of no talk, since every message means another model call that re-reads the battle and the conversation so far.

I also checked that the environment can tell models apart. A Qwen3.8-27B team won 96% of its battles against a team of 2B models and 74% against a team of 9B models, compared with 64% against the max-damage bot. The stronger the opponent, the closer the games, which is what makes the environment usable as a benchmark for comparing models.

I'm separating the effect of talking from the effect of seeing your partner's move. I'm also looking into turning the environment into a benchmark with a leaderboard across models, and using it for RL training to encourage collaborative behaviors.

Through this project I wanted to learn more about agent collaboration and RL environments, and thought I'd share the results! I ran these experiments on Texas A&M's Grace cluster. Thank you to Maria Teleki and to my advisor, Prof. James Caverlee , for the guidance and feedback along the way.

items.title: US orders some diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate
items.summary: The warning to US officials comes as at least three people die in the latest strikes at an airport and an oil field.
items.content:
The US State Department has ordered some diplomats and their families to leave Saudi Arabia as attacks escalate, with three people killed in strikes across the country.

Saudi authorities said debris from a drone intercepted during an attempted attack on an oil field killed two people, while one person died after a strike at the King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.

Conflict between Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi Arabia has been rising in the past month.

The Houthis have responded to Saudi strikes by launching missiles and drones at airports, energy facilities and military bases in Saudi Arabia. A recent strike on Riyadh's international airport was the deadliest in the kingdom in years.

"The US Department of State issued an ordered departure for non-emergency US government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia," a state department spokesperson said in a statement.

"Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," it added.

The spokesperson also warned "the hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly".

In the latest attack on the King Fahd International Airport eight people sustained injuries that ranged from "minor to serious", officials said.

No details of the attack have yet been given, but the strike comes after airports in Saudi Arabia have been repeatedly targeted by Houthi forces.

The energy ministry has also not said who had launched the drone aimed at the Shaybah oil field near the border with the United Arab Emirates that left two people injured.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began when the Houthis ousted the government from the capital, Sanaa, in 2014. Conflicts escalated in 2015, after a Saudi-led military coalition tried to restore the government's rule.

An informal ceasefire had been in place for the past four years, but it unravelled in July after the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they have called a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

The group's "maritime embargo" in the Bab al-Mandab Strait along Yemen's south-western coast has contributed to a surge in global oil prices because Saudi Arabia had been relying on the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.

UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

items.title: Roborock Saros 20 Neo è il robot aspirapolvere lavapavimenti che toglie di mezzo anche gli imprevisti
items.summary: Tanta automazione, stazione multifunzione e aspirazione da 36.000 Pa. Perché la vera innovazione è dover fare meno per la pulizia ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
I robot aspirapolvere hanno già risolto da tempo il problema più semplice: muoversi per casa raccogliendo polvere e sporco. Ciò che continua a fare la differenza, soprattutto nella fascia più alta del mercato, è tutto ciò che accade quando la casa smette di essere un ambiente ideale.

In pratica, quando ci sono i vari, piccoli ostacoli che sono comuni in un’abitazione normale: come un tappeto più spesso di un altro, una soglia alta o un cavo lasciato a terra. Oppure, semplicemente, la necessità di lavare e asciugare i mop senza che qualcuno debba intervenire ogni volta.

Roborock Saros 20 Neo è un robot che abbina 36.000 Pa di aspirazione a una serie di soluzioni pensate soprattutto per ridurre le situazioni nelle quali l’utente è costretto a preparare la casa prima della pulizia o a intervenire durante il ciclo. In altre parole, è un robot pensato per occuparsi anche degli imprevisti.

Ma c'è un altro motivo: Saros 20 Neo è in sconto a 749 euro su Amazon e sull'eshop di Roborock.

Uno dei limiti più evidenti dei robot aspirapolvere emerge quando incontrano dislivelli, soglie e tappeti. Per superarli, Saros 20 Neo utilizza il sistema AdaptiLift 3.0, progettato per modificare l’assetto del robot in base a ciò che trova davanti a sé. Nell’attività di pulizia permette quindi di superare soglie doppie alte complessivamente fino a 8,8 centimetri , suddivise in due passaggi da 4,5 e 4,3 centimetri. Il sistema è stato progettato per resistere a oltre 20.000 attraversamenti delle soglie, che equivalgono ad anni di pulizia quotidiana.

In più, Saros 20 Neo può sollevare il proprio assetto e gestire tappeti con pelo fino a 3 centimetri . Quando invece il lavaggio rischierebbe di rappresentare un problema oppure si è deciso di aspirare prima i tappeti attraverso l’apposita funzione, i mop vengono rimossi automaticamente quando il robot parte dalla base multifunzione, evitando così di trascinare superfici bagnate sopra i tappeti. Invece attivando la modalità di pulizia profonda dei tappeti, la spazzola principale del Saros 20 Neo rimane in posizione stabile verso il basso durante una seconda passata, per migliorare la raccolta dei detriti rispetto alla normale posizione flottante.

La potenza di aspirazione HyperForce raggiunge i 36.000 Pa , perfetta per aspirare lo sporco anche negli angoli, anche grazie all’inclusione del braccio laterale FlexiArm Arc può estendersi verso l’esterno per raggiungere più facilmente i bordi. A ciò si aggiunge il sistema Dual Anti-Tangle, che lavora insieme alla spazzola DuoDivide per limitare l’accumulo di capelli e peli. Insomma: Saros 20 Neo lascia il pavimento pulito e ordinato e poi non c’è bisogno di perdere tempo a rimuovere i capelli rimasti avvolti nella spazzola.

Per il lavaggio, Saros 20 Neo utilizza due mop rotanti che possono raggiungere una velocità di 200 giri al minuto e applicare fino a 14 N di pressione sul pavimento. Inoltre, Saros 20 Neo riduce fino al 30% l’acqua residua lasciata sul pavimento.

Prima ancora di aspirare o lavare, il robot deve capire che cosa ha davanti. Saros 20 Neo utilizza il sistema Reactive AI Obstacle Recognition, basato su fotocamera RGB e luce strutturata, insieme alla tecnologia VertiBeam.

Grazie a questo sistema avanzato, può riconoscere oggetti comuni che possono trovarsi sul pavimento, come cavi, scarpe, giocattoli, ciotole e altri piccoli ostacoli.

Per anni, uno dei consigli più comuni prima di avviare un robot aspirapolvere è stato togliere da terra tutto ciò che potrebbe confonderlo. Un prodotto come Saros 20 Neo ribalta invece il problema: è il robot che deve imparare a gestire ciò che trova; e il Saros 20 Neo ci riesce molto bene.

Allo scopo di adattare il robot alle esigenze domestiche e non viceversa, Saros 20 Neo misura 7,98 centimetri in altezza. Può sembrare una caratteristica meno evidente e impattante rispetto ai 36.000 Pa di aspirazione, ma le sue dimensioni gli permettono di passare facilmente sotto ai divani e ai letti oltre che sotto i mobili bassi fino a 7,95 cm, che spesso sono fra le zone più complicate per i robot dotati di torrette di navigazione più alte.

Saros 20 Neo ci riesce perché il sistema di scansione dell’ambiente circostante, che normalmente è sollevato per garantire una mappatura precisa, viene automaticamente ritratto e passa a una visuale posteriore a 100°: così il robot continua a sapere come muoversi ma può passare anche in spazi dove altri dispositivi non arrivano.

Ancora più interessante è il modo in cui il robot gestisce la differenza fra una stanza e l’altra. Con SmartPlan 3.0, Saros 20 Neo può adattare il ciclo di pulizia tenendo conto della tipologia di ambiente , dei materiali e dello storico delle sessioni precedenti. Per esempio, può intensificare la pulizia nelle aree che sono state trascurate oppure tornare alla base per lavare nuovamente i mop dopo essere passato in cucina o in bagno.

Inoltre, il Saros 20 Neo sa occuparsi anche di zone della casa che normalmente rischiano di essere trascurate. Contrassegnando manualmente le tende, per esempio, pulisce dietro tende e divisori morbidi, coprendo quindi anche le aree nascosto senza bisogno di sollevarli o regolarli. E quando le porte di una stanza sono chiuse, il Saros 20 Neo prosegue senza urtarle né spingerle, per evitare il rischio di danneggiarle. E se in precedenza ha evitato una zona - magari perché c’era un ostacolo temporaneo o un animale domestico - il sistema è progettato per proseguire l’attività di pulizia altrove e poi ritorna sulla zona non coperta appena è libera. Per di più, SmartPlan 3.0 è un sistema che continua a imparare dalle abitudini di pulizia e quindi migliora nel tempo.

Non è solo il robot a essere dotato di grande autonomia, perché anche la base multifunzione riesce a compiere tante operazioni senza bisogno di intervento. La base multifunzione infatti può svuotare automaticamente il contenitore della polvere, lavare i mop con acqua fino a 100 °C (rimuovendo il 99,99% dei batteri) e asciugarli successivamente con aria calda fino a 55 °C.

Il sistema può anche rilevare il livello di sporco dei mop e decidere di prolungarne il lavaggio oppure richiedere al robot un ulteriore passaggio nell’area appena pulita. Sono previste anche il riempimento automatico con acqua calda e il dosaggio del detergente.

La parte interna della base è rimovibile, così da semplificarne la pulizia quando necessario. È forse qui che si vede meglio il cambiamento avvenuto in questa categoria di prodotti.

Una parte della gestione rimane comunque nelle mani dell’utente. Attraverso l’app Roborock è possibile lavorare sulle mappe, dividere gli ambienti, creare zone escluse, scegliere modalità e intensità della pulizia oppure definire il comportamento sui tappeti.

Anche i comandi vocali possono essere utilizzati direttamente attraverso "Hello Rocky" , anche senza Wi-Fi, che permette di avviare o interrompere la pulizia, indicare una stanza, localizzare il robot oppure modificare aspirazione e quantità d’acqua. Il sistema può funzionare anche offline. Inoltre, supporta il protocollo Matter, che consente di automatizzare le routine e controllare i vari dispositivi della smart home da un’unica piattaforma, che sia Alexa, Siri o Google Home.

In questa puntata parliamo di AI Sound Controller Pro , la tecnologia che utilizza l’intelligenza artificiale per riconoscere gli elementi di una colonna sonora, separarli e permetterti di regolarli come piace a te.

AI Sound Controller Pro è una delle funzionalità della modalità AI degli Vision AI Smart TV di Samsung. La modalità AI offre diverse funzioni che ottimizzano le immagini e i suoni in base al contenuto e all’ambiente in cui è installato il tuo televisore. Utilizza algoritmi di intelligenza artificiale per analizzare il contenuto in riproduzione e migliorare la resa.

AI Sound Controller Pro è una delle funzioni più sofisticate e utilizza l’IA per consentirti di personalizzare non semplicemente la qualità del suono ma il vero e proprio missaggio del contenuto: grazie ad AI Sound Controller Pro puoi infatti andare a regolare con precisione il livello dei vari elementi della colonna sonora , creando il mix più adatto alle tue esigenze.

Preferisci avere dialoghi maggiormente in evidenza e gli effetti sonori meno roboanti? Oppure c’è una bella canzone e la vuoi sentire più chiaramente? Con AI Sound Controller Pro puoi finalmente aggiustare i livelli separatamente con qualsiasi tipo di contenuto.

AI Sound Controller Pro utilizza l’intelligenza artificiale per analizzare il contenuto audio e individuare e separare i dialoghi dalla musica e da tutti gli altri suoni . Il tutto avviene automaticamente, basta attivare la modalità AI. Stai guardando un bel film di guerra e il rumore dell’artiglieria non ti fa sentire bene i dialoghi? Non c’è problema.

Nel menù dedicato ad AI Sound Controller Pro troverai gli intuitivi slider già dedicati a voce, musica ed effetti sonori. Ed è qui che avviene la magia: grazie a questi controlli potrai infatti regolare a piacere il volume dei dialoghi, della musica e degli effetti sonori . Puoi quindi ad esempio scegliere di aumentare il volume delle voci, e contemporaneamente abbassare quello degli effetti sonori, delle musiche o entrambi.

Puoi sbizzarrirti adattando il mix del suono come preferisci fino a quando trovi il bilanciamento migliore per te e puoi confrontare semplicemente il prima e il dopo attivando e disattivando la modalità AI per sentire la differenza.

items.title: Alfa Romeo Stelvio e trazione Q4: l'agilità del posteriore con la sicurezza del 4x4
items.summary: La trazione Q4 di Alfa Romeo Stelvio non è come le altre: tutti i vantaggi di un sistema intelligente ed efficace, nato dal DNA Alfa ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Molti SUV a trazione integrale soffrono dello stesso limite: per garantire stabilità su fondi scivolosi, sacrificano l'agilità, risultando pesanti e poco reattivi in curva. Alfa Romeo supera questo limite ingegneristico progettando un'architettura a trazione posteriore nativa con inserimento predittivo dell'asse anteriore. Un esempio concreto di questa tecnologia è la trazione integrale Q4 presente su Alfa Romeo Stelvio, un sistema che unisce il dinamismo della trazione posteriore al margine di aderenza di un 4x4.

A differenza delle piattaforme basate su trazione anteriore permanente, la logica della trazione Q4 mantiene la priorità di spinta sul retrotreno, gestendo la coppia attraverso componenti meccanici ed elaborazione dati in tempo reale:

L'efficacia del sistema Q4 su Alfa Romeo Stelvio è legata all'impiego di materiali e soluzioni ingegneristiche avanzate concepite per ridurre le masse in movimento:

L'eccellenza della tecnologia Q4 si riassume in quattro caratteristiche costruttive ideate per garantire la massima efficienza e il totale controllo del veicolo:

Come funziona il sistema di trazione integrale Q4 di Alfa Romeo?

Il sistema Q4 utilizza un ripartitore di coppia attivo (ATC) abbinato a un albero di trasmissione in fibra di carbonio. In condizioni di guida ordinarie, l'auto funziona con trazione al 100% posteriore. Monitorando costantemente parametri come accelerazione laterale, angolo di sterzo e slittamento, la centralina trasmette fino al 50% della forza motrice all'asse anteriore in circa 150 millisecondi.

Quali sono i vantaggi del sistema Q4 rispetto a un 4x4 tradizionale?

A differenza dei sistemi 4x4 tradizionali a trazione anteriore o permanente, la tecnologia Q4 riduce il peso complessivo del veicolo attenuando la tendenza al sottosterzo e rendendo l'inserimento in curva più immediato. Inoltre, trasferendo la coppia all'avantreno solo quando strettamente necessario, riduce gli attriti parassiti e ottimizza il consumo di carburante nell'impiego autostradale e urbano.

La tecnologia Q4 è disponibile su tutte le motorizzazioni della Stelvio?

La trazione integrale Q4 è abbinata alle principali motorizzazioni Turbo Benzina e Turbo Diesel di potenza elevata della gamma Alfa Romeo Stelvio, sempre in coppia con il cambio automatico a 8 rapporti.

La tecnologia Q4 è disponibile anche sugli altri SUV Alfa Romeo?

Sì. Sebbene Alfa Romeo Stelvio rappresenti la massima espressione meccanica del sistema con trazione posteriore nativa e albero in fibra di carbonio, la tecnologia di trazione integrale Q4 è stata declinata su tutta la gamma SUV adattandosi alle diverse architetture:

items.title: Come scegliere il caricatore USB-C giusto (eh no, non sono tutti uguali)
items.summary: Scegliere un caricatore? Semplice, alla fine hanno tutti lo stesso connettore USB-C. Peccato che non sia così: cavi diversi, sigle diverse, potenze diverse ma alimentatori esteriormente molto simili tra loro: la scelta di un caricatore non è sempre facile. Perché se è vero che oggi con un solo alimentatore si può caricare di tutto, è anche vero che deve essere scelto bene. ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Alzi la mano chi non ha in casa un cassetto pieno di cavi ingarbugliati e di caricatori. Un alimentatore per il telefono, uno per il notebook, uno per il tablet, ognuno con la sua spina e, nel caso di prodotti meno recenti, anche con un connettore proprietario. Oggi, per fortuna, il cassetto si sta progressivamente svuotando grazie all'unione di due tasselli: da un lato lo standard USB-C Power Delivery, che permette a un solo alimentatore di erogare potenze diverse a seconda del dispositivo collegato, e dall'altro la normativa europea che ha spinto tutti i produttori ad abbandonare i connettori proprietari in favore dell'USB-C come connettore universale.

Il risultato è da un lato che oggi insieme agli apparecchi quasi sempre non viene più incluso l'alimentatore; ma dall'altro lato è vero che, nella maggior parte dei casi, un unico caricatore può bastare per smartphone, tablet, cuffie, console portatili e persino per il notebook (sempre che questo non sia un laptop da gaming che ha richieste particolari in termini di potenza).

Nonostante questo, scegliere un alimentatore non è semplicissimo, anche se dovrebbe esserlo: il fatto che il connettore USB-C si infili nell'alimentatore non basta a garantire una ricarica veloce, o addirittura la ricarica nel caso di dispositivi energivori. Questa guida, realizzata in collaborazione con Techly , è pensata per spiegare, dalla A alla Z, tutto quello che c'è da sapere per scegliere il caricatore perfetto.

La sigla USB-C indica semplicemente la forma di quel connettore, che ormai dovrebbe essere familiare, ovale e utilizzabile da entrambi i lati. Power Delivery, spesso abbreviato in PD, è invece il protocollo che regola quanta energia viene trasferita attraverso quel connettore: il caricatore non eroga indistintamente la stessa potenza a tutti i dispositivi, ma comunica con l’apparecchio collegato e regola automaticamente l’energia in uscita, assicurando la massima velocità di ricarica compatibile con entrambi. Un alimentatore Power Delivery negozia con il dispositivo collegato una serie di profili di tensione, solitamente 5, 9, 12, 15 o 20 Volt, scegliendo quello più adatto per ricaricare un prodotto al meglio. Per questo la prima cosa da cercare quando si sceglie un caricatore non è solo la porta USB-C, quella ormai ce l'hanno tutti, ma la dicitura specifica USB-C PD 3.2 (l'ultima versione dello standard), che è quella che garantisce la compatibilità con il più ampio numero di dispositivi possibili. Un laptop, ad esempio, ha bisogno di 20 Volt, che un alimentatore da smartphone classico non può erogare, mentre la Nintendo Switch, tanto per fare un esempio, ha bisogno di 15 Volt.

La seconda domanda che solitamente una persona si fa è: "Quanti Watt mi servono?". Sebbene la tentazione sia quella di prendere sempre l'alimentatore con il numero più alto disponibile, è probabilmente più indicato ragionare per fasce e secondo le necessità, perché a potenza più elevata corrisponde un caricatore non solo più costoso ma anche più pesante e ingombrante.

Esiste tuttavia un modo per avere un caricatore che sia potente ma al tempo stesso compatto: basta scegliere un caricatore GaN . Sostituendo il silicio con il nitruro di gallio (GaN) nei componenti interni, materiale che permette di gestire le stesse potenze con meno dispersione di calore e quindi con dimensioni molto più contenute, le aziende sono riuscite a costruire caricatori per laptop piccoli come quelli tradizionali per smartphone. Il che da un lato è un evidente vantaggio, ma dall'altro può ingenerare ulteriore confusione: la dimensione dell'alimentatore non può essere presa più come "metro" della sua potenza.

L' IPW-PD65W , ad esempio, è un alimentatore da 65 Watt che pesa poco e sta tranquillamente in tasca. I modelli GaN sono leggermente più costosi, ma valgono la spesa.

Questo è, per esempio, un caricatore da 20 W (esiste anche in versione da 30 W) adatto per smartphone e piccoli dispositivi.

Questo alimentatore dispone di due porte, una USB-C e una USB-A così da essere adatto a qualsiasi cavo e distribuisce la sua potenza sulle due porte.

Collegando solo un device, tutta la potenza verrà destinata a quell'apparecchio, secondo le combinazioni di tensioni e potenze scritte sull'alimentatore.

Salendo a 30 W, come con questo alimentatore , che è anche GaN, si guadagna un po' di margine anche su tablet più esigenti e alcuni notebook ultraleggeri.

La tecnologia GaN permette comunque di mantenere le dimensioni compatte, rendendolo un apparecchio adatto anche per i viaggi. Non a caso si tratta di un vero "best seller" del sito Techly, anche in considerazione del costo contenuto.

L'erogazione di potenza massima è 30W, disponibili (una per volta) su entrambe le porte, anche quella USB-A. Nel caso di utilizzo contemporaneo di entrambe le uscite, cosa comunque possibile, la potenza su ogni porta si dimezza.

La soglia dei 45 W è quella che comincia a coprire i notebook più sottili, anche se con qualche compromesso nei carichi di lavoro intensi, mentre il vero salto arriva a 65 W, la potenza che oggi rappresenta il taglio più versatile in assoluto: come vedremo, riesce a ricaricare praticamente ogni dispositivo di uso quotidiano, incluso un MacBook Air o la maggior parte degli ultrabook Windows.

Questo modello (disponibile anche nella variante da 45 W) ha una sola uscita USB-C ma è stupefacente per dimensioni contenute e efficienza, tanto che, anche durante la ricarica, si scalda molto poco.

Si arriva infine a 100 W (o superiori), necessari solo per workstation portatili o per chi vuole ricaricare rapidamente due dispositivi impegnativi contemporaneamente dalla stessa presa, perché, come abbiamo detto, la potenza indicata per i caricatori con più prese USB-C è quella aggregata e non quella erogabile dalla singola presa.

Il modello IPW-PD100W-2A2CW, per esempio, è un GaN da 100 W e dispone di 4 porte di uscita, due USB-C e due USB-A.

Ma attenzione, in questo caso (è ben specificato nei dettagli tecnici) collegando un solo device alla prima porta USB-C è possibile ottenere tutti i 100W con una connessione a 20V e 5 A, per esempio per caricare un MacBook Pro o una workstation potente; se invece si attaccano più device insieme, la potenza si distribuisce secondo alcuni schemi: per esempio 65 + 20 W sulle due porte USB-C; o 65 + 18 sulle due USB-A.

Chi vuole il massimo della versatilità, invece, sempre rimanendo sui modelli "a muro", può trovare la propria soluzione nel caricatore IPW-PD140W-WH da 140 W.

Le porte sono quattro, tre USB-C e una USB-A, mix che rispecchia meglio la natura dei device attuali.

Collegando un solo PC alla USB-C, si erogano appunto fino a 140W secondo gli standard Power Delivery.

Ma anche collegando, per esempio, due MacBook Air, si ottengono 65 W ciascuno, quanto basta per alimentarli entrambi.

Oppure si possono fare altri mix usando tutte le quattro porte, che consentono di alimentare e caricare per esempio un PC, un tablet, uno smartphone e uno smartwatch, tutto con dimensioni e pesi molto contenuti.

Ne giova anche l'ordine di casa: niente ciabatte e niente diversi caricabatterie.

Spesso si pensa che sia solo l'alimentatore a decidere quanta potenza deve arrivare al dispositivo, ma non è così: anche il cavo ha un limite di potenza che può trasportare. Correnti elevate, infatti, porterebbero i cavi più sottili a scaldarsi, quindi con alcuni cavi le potenze vengono limitate in automatico. È questo il motivo per il quale molti smartphone con sistemi di ricarica veloce, anche 120 Watt, vengono venduti con il loro cavo (e richiedono il loro caricatore): certe tecnologie di ricarica proprietarie richiedono la corretta combinazione di cavo e alimentatore. Non tutti i cavi, infatti, sono progettati per reggere i 240 Watt massimi che l'USB-C supporta: molti dei cavi "semplici" in circolazione si fermano a 60 W, e alcuni addirittura a potenze inferiori, anche se il connettore è identico e sembra funzionare normalmente. Il risultato, nel migliore dei casi, è una ricarica più lenta di quanto il caricatore potrebbe offrire; nel peggiore, un cavo non certificato di provenienza dubbia può scaldarsi eccessivamente sotto carico prolungato.

Come fa un cavo a ridurre la potenza del caricatore? I cavi USB-C più evoluti integrano un piccolo chip chiamato e-marker, che comunica al caricatore le caratteristiche reali del cavo, dalla potenza massima alla velocità dati. Per chi ha un Mac, esiste WhatCable, un'applicazione gratuita e open source che legge questi dati e segnala in modo chiaro se un cavo sta "limitando" la ricarica rispetto a quanto il caricatore potrebbe erogare. Se avete nel cassetto un po' di cavi, WhatCable può essere utile per etichettarli: "smartphone", "tablet", "pc" e così via.

Sul sito Techly, nella descrizione dei tantissimi cavi USB-C disponibili (tutti rigorosamente a norma), è chiaramente indicata la potenza di ricarica gestita.

Il codice ICOC MU4-40G240W1 , per esempio, è uno dei più completi e, non solo è in grado di trasferire dati fino a 40 Gbps, ma gestisce ricariche secondo lo standard Power Delivery 3.1 fino a 240 W di potenza. Praticamente ci fai tutto.

items.title: iRobot è così sicura dei suoi Roomba da farteli provare a casa per 30 giorni
items.summary: Il Roomba si porta a casa, si mette al lavoro sui propri pavimenti e, se non convince, si restituisce entro 30 giorni con il rimborso del prezzo pagato. Vale anche sui modelli in offerta ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Un robot aspirapolvere si sceglie leggendo le schede, ma si giudica solo a casa propria, tra il divano e il tappeto del soggiorno. Per questo iRobot ha deciso di togliere di mezzo il dubbio. Chi compra un Roomba ha 30 giorni per provarlo nella vita di tutti i giorni e, se non lo convince, lo restituisce e riceve indietro i soldi. Il programma si chiama Soddisfatti o Rimborsati e sarà attivo fino al 31 marzo 2027 .

Dietro c'è un ragionamento semplice. Un'azienda propone una prova così lunga solo quando è convinta che, dopo un mese di pulizie, il robot si sarà guadagnato il suo posto in casa.

Passerà sotto il letto? E sul tappeto a pelo lungo si arrampicherà o rimarrà impigliato? Riuscirà a stare dietro al pelo del gatto che cambia stagione? Come laverà il mio parquet? Sono le domande che si fa chiunque stia per comprare un robot , e nessuna scheda tecnica può rispondere per una casa che non conosce.

Trenta giorni bastano per scoprirlo . In pochissimo tempo un Roomba impara la pianta dell'appartamento e si abitua a soglie e bordi dei tappeti, passando dal parquet del soggiorno alle piastrelle del bagno. Chi ha animali lo vede al lavoro nei giorni normali, quelli in cui il pelo si accumula negli angoli e sotto i mobili. E chi vuole avere sempre un pavimento lavato di fresco potrà testare anche le capacità di lavare e asciugare il rullo del robot sulla base AutoWash dei modelli che la prevedono, per evitare muffe e cattivi odori.

È anche il modo migliore per apprezzare i Roomba più recenti . Il 115 e i Plus 415, 515 e 575 hanno un profilo fino al 21% più sottile del Roomba Plus 505. Se sulla carta è un numero, sotto il proprio divano diventa la polvere che finalmente sparisce.

Il meccanismo è pensato per non complicare la vita a chi compra.

1. Si acquista il Roomba da un qualunque rivenditore, in negozio oppure online.

2. Entro 10 giorni dall'acquisto lo si registra su irobot.it , caricando lo scontrino o la conferma d'ordine.

3. Si usa il robot in casa , come si farebbe con qualunque elettrodomestico appena comprato.

4. Se non convince, entro 30 giorni dall'acquisto si chiede il reso dalla propria area riservata . Un corriere passa a ritirarlo senza costi e il prezzo pagato torna con un bonifico.

L'unica accortezza è conservare la scatola originale e lo scontrino , perché il Roomba torna indietro completo, come è arrivato.

La prova vale anche quando il Roomba si compra in promozione. Chi approfitta di uno sconto da un rivenditore conserva i suoi 30 giorni e, in caso di reso, riceve indietro quanto ha effettivamente pagato. Restano fuori soltanto i Roomba ottenuti come omaggio, per esempio in un'offerta 3x2, o vinti come premio di un concorso.

Con le offerte di ottobre ancora in corso , è il momento più conveniente per mettere un Roomba alla prova .

Sul negozio ufficiale di iRobot i 30 giorni ci sono già "di serie", per ogni acquisto . Chi ordina da irobot.it non deve registrarsi al programma. Se il robot non lo convince, lo restituisce con la normale procedura di reso del sito, entro 30 giorni dalla consegna.

Il programma non si limita a qualche modello di punta. Comprende i Roomba d'ingresso come il 115 , i Plus delle serie 400, 500 e 600, i Max delle serie 700 e 800, fino al Mini Combo. Valgono anche le versioni proposte su Amazon. L'unica condizione è che il robot sia nuovo e distribuito in Italia da Nital, con il Sigillo di Garanzia Ufficiale Italia sulla confezione.

Se ci si vuole affidare a punti vendita fisici, il rivenditore più vicino si trova con la ricerca dei rivenditori di iRobot , mentre la pagina del programma spiega come registrarsi . Per l'elenco completo dei modelli e tutte le condizioni del rimborso conviene leggere il regolamento .

items.title: The real reasons US politicians are getting older
items.summary: No country for young men and women: why do older politicians seem to have such a tight grip on the US political system?
items.content:
Not many US politicians have endured for as long as Hal Rogers, who will go into November's midterm elections seeking his 24th term in the House of Representatives.

The 88-year-old Republican has represented Kentucky's 5th congressional district since 1981, making him the longest serving member of the House of Representatives. He was elected on the same night Ronald Reagan won his first presidential term under the slogan "Let's make America great again", a phrase later revived by Donald Trump.

Among the challengers Rogers beat to win the nomination this year was one 60 years his junior. But Rogers, born in the 1930s, is far from the only senior US politician to have stuck at the job into their 80s.

Others to have done so include US President Donald Trump, 80; Trump's predecessor Joe Biden, who left office at 82; and Nancy Pelosi, who stepped down as the Democratic leader in the House at the same age. Chuck Grassley, 93, is still a senator. He entered politics in 1958, before Alaska and Hawaii were even US states.

The age and health of some politicians has raised widespread concern within both Republican and Democratic circles, however, reigniting questions about whether age limits or health checks should be imposed.

The US is well known for its "gerontocracy", a government ruled by people who are significantly older than most of the adult population.

At the other end of the age spectrum, the US has one of the lowest proportions of lawmakers under the age of 45 among comparable democracies, according to research from the Inter-Parliamentary Union.

So why are so few young people becoming politicians? And for those who do enter politics, can they make a success of it?

Twenty-seven-year-old Republican Riley Owen is one of the few candidates from Gen Z - aged in their early teens to late 20s - from either party running for Congress on 3 November.

Owen is running in a newly created district in Utah that experts say may lean towards the Democrats. He has championed issues including paid maternity leave, restrictions on congressional stock trading and environmental action - all issues that may appeal to Democratic supporters.

When he was confirmed as his party's candidate in the state's 1st congressional district, he walked on stage to Billy Joel's We Didn't Start the Fire, and argued that his generation needed to help renew the American Dream.

The gerontocracy is "a bipartisan issue", he says. "We've got people who have become career politicians, and they spend their lives in Congress." He says this is indicative of a system that is not delivering for Americans.

Owen says the big challenge he faces is the fact that money really talks in US politics. Research suggests campaign donors tend to prefer incumbent candidates.

Indeed, the campaign of his rival Ben McAdams - a 51-year-old Democrat who has previously served in Congress - has so far raised much more cash than Owen's. By mid-October, McAdams had raised over $2.6m (£1.9m), compared with $150,000 raised by Owen, according to records on the Federal Election Commission website.

Owen argues that his generation is uniquely well-placed to understand contemporary political issues, such as the challenges posed by tech. He also disputes any suggestion that a younger candidate necessarily lacks relevant experience - pointing to his own background as a military officer and a White House policy analyst. "I think in politics, just like in industry, we need what's called disruptive innovation," he says.

The age of America's top politicians has long been a talking point. In 1984 Reagan - who was then America's oldest president at age 73 - deflected scrutiny with a quip about the "youth and inexperience" of his opponent Walter Mondale, who was a sprightly 56.

In the US, individual states also have their own legislatures, with a Senate and a House, where many politicians make their start. Many current members of Congress spent years in state politics before running for a seat in Washington

But the median age of Congress members has ticked upwards over time. Congressional records show that the lowest median ages in the House and Senate were both recorded in the early 1980s - at 48 and 52 respectively.

The average ages of a House member and a senator at the start of the current Congress were 58 and 65 respectively, according to analysis by the Pew Research Center. The median age of a US citizen is 39.

There is now also a sharper focus on the health and acuity of some of the nation's oldest politicians. Joe Biden's age became a major issue while he was in office. To a lesser extent Trump has faced questions too.

So too has Republican Senator Mitch McConnell, 84, with increasing regularity, after a months-long absence from Congress to undergo medical treatment. Meanwhile, on the Democratic side, Maxine Waters, 88, faces a leadership challenge as the lead Democrat on the powerful House Financial Services Committee, with her age considered by some to be a factor counting against her.

Some of the most vocal critics of this so-called gerontocracy have been candidates who identify as democratic socialists, meaning that their political views are further to the left than those of the Democratic Party mainstream. These candidates tend to campaign heavily on the cost of living and other issues that cut through to Millennials and Gen Z, and their supporters skew younger too.

The demographic profile of people who vote tends to skew older, like the elected officials themselves. Pew research highlights that the proportion of non-voters who are young (aged 18 to 29) has been increasing. In the 2020 US election, 25% of non-voters belonged to that age category, according to Pew. Four years later, it had risen to 30%.

Pew adds that voters under 30 were underrepresented in 2024. Voters in that age category made up 20% of the voting-eligible population, though accounted for only 15% of all the votes that were actually cast.

Campaigners argue that these demographic trends matter because they leave some issues underrepresented.

"Yes, that might result in older people being elected, but I think it really skews, too, what issues are important; what issues politicians are incentivised to talk about and to take care of," says Grace Mausser, the co-chair of the New York City wing of the Democratic Socialists of America.

Mausser campaigned for Zohran Mamdani in his winning bid last year to become, at age 34, New York City's youngest mayor since 1892. Mamdani was held up as an example of a rare youthful success story, but his ally Mausser is less concerned with a politician's age than with their outlook.

Mausser says it is not necessarily a problem if someone has been in politics for a long time. Rather, the problem can be what may result from that: "You become so used to the language and the ideas of the political establishment that anything else - any new ideas, whether they come from young people or old people - seem crazy."

She invokes left-wing Democratic senator Bernie Sanders, 85, as an example of an older politician with a long tenure on Capitol Hill who has embraced change and had ideas that have resonated across generations.

In the US, older people hold politicians in far higher esteem than younger people - even more so than in many other countries, according to a Pew survey from spring 2025. Some 62% of 18-34-year-olds were likely to say few or none of their elected officials are honest, compared with 45% of people aged over 50. Of the 25 countries surveyed by Pew, only Greece's young adults had a more pessimistic view of the honesty of politicians.

For one expert who studies political engagement on both sides of the Atlantic, disaffection among young people helps to explain their unwillingness to participate in politics. The issue is not helped by the fact Congress has minimum age requirements for members, he says. Candidates must be 30 to serve as a senator, and 25 to be a representative.

"The one leads to another," remarks James Sloam from Royal Holloway, University of London. "If you don't have enough young people engaged in politics generally, then they won't become representatives."

What is more, Sloam says, young people in the US and the UK alike are alert to the fact that power does not just lie in politics. They are aware there are many other areas of work in which they can wield influence - including over elected officials.

For those young people who do end up in high-profile political positions, the next question is whether they can make a success of it, especially when it comes to parenthood. Over the summer, the stories of two high-profile young women working in Washington raised fresh questions around compatibility of the job with motherhood.

Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, 37, a Democratic congresswoman who took office aged 29, announced that she had started the process of freezing her eggs.

Later the same week in August, Karoline Leavitt, 29, who was appointed the youngest ever White House press secretary almost two years earlier, said she would leave the Trump administration to spend more time with her family, including her newborn baby. She explained: "I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy and attention required of [being] the White House press secretary."

items.title: There isn't an easy exploit for this PHP vulnerability
items.summary: Article URL: https://eliastaylor.com/noexploit/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50188948 Points: 366 # Comments: 171
items.content:
I know, I know. It's all you're hearing about. That, and the number 4 .

Don't get me wrong, there's clearly a bug here and it really does matter. But this is not easy to exploit. It is certainly nowhere near as eay as Log4Shell/Heartbleed/RoRYaml etc.

I don't think this PHP vulnerability is that exploitable. I think that 5 years ago people would've understood this, but now people are being deluded by their LLMs telling them they have an exploit when they don't.

If you take a look at github right now, there are thousands, literally thousands, of "PoC" exploits for this vulnerability. One thing you'll notice about all of them though, is that they do not work against a vanilla PHP instance.

Go ahead, stand up a php server you think is vulnerable in Docker and then run the PoC yourself . Don't get your LLM to do it. No. Run the script, yourself. The exploits don't work.

I think that a lot of people had assumed that LLMs will be able to build an exploit chain instantly from reading the diff, and that even if this was harder to exploit than other exploits, LLMs would've levelled the playing field. Well. There's no working exploit. Now what?

When I think about "we're very fucked" CVE10s on the Internet, I think of the following vulnerabilities:

The second these vulnerabilities made the news, there were botnets doing the rounds causing damage. And this was before LLMs! People have to write the botnets. With their hands!

It's been 10 hours since this vulnerability has been posted, and half the software world is looking at it, and lord knows 100,000 people have got their "superintelligence" on the case. Nevertheless, there's no working exploit. The ones doing the rounds are fake, or only work in a lab, because...

Script kiddies (and script adults, who have also switched their brains off) now all think that, well, they don't understand UAF chaining, but this Claude guy knows everything and can totally make an exploit.

Hilariously, this results in the LLM giving their younger-brother an unplugged controller. It says exploit all across the screen... and has some smoking gun transcripts... but it's modified the server you're testing against to have a severe vulnerability. Cheating!!

One really amusing thing in common with most of these "PoC"s is that they lean on "LFI", or local-file-inclusion, to make the vulnerability. In non-php terms, their exploit chain requires the server to effectively do eval(read(filename_provided_by_user)) .

It's not rare for PHP apps to be fucked in some sense, but requiring the server to have an existing vulnerability where one could cat /etc/password is an insane pre-requisite. If you need this, this does not make this a severe bug.

The strangest thing is that so many people have independently made this extraordinarily weird defect in judgement. That is because they haven't independently made this decision. Claude/Etc. has done all of the judgement for them, hence the bizarre distribution in logical errors.

There's something important to be said here about how many people have Claude/GPT make design decisions for them, and how AI is the primary decision maker in the world right now. You've got this bizarre case of "Decision Schelling Points" where a method of solving a problem is extremely overrepresented, because it's what Claude does out of the box.

This is annoying in the case of "most websites look the same now", but because LLMs have the power to ruin every domain at the same time, this is also "most decisions are suspiciously the same now". Especially in this case, where AI is inserting a vulnerability on the server... to prove that the server is vulnerable to your "exploit any PHP instance" attack!

And we've had things like this before, but not in the LLM era yet. Luckily for us, this doesn't seem to be that day. This is too difficult to exploit easily. It isn't a Log4J moment.

items.title: Trump's green card curbs test Indian tech workers' American dream
items.summary: With immigration curbs and tech firms cutting foreign hiring, US residency is becoming a distant dream for many Indians.
items.content:
For millions of Indians, the road to the ultimate career aspiration had a familiar script - an engineering degree to get a tech services job, then a posting in the US, repeated visa renewals and then the green card that gave them permanent residency in the country.

Earlier this month, the US announced it would suspend eight technology firms , including Microsoft, India's Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro and HCL Technologies, from hiring skilled international workers on a permanent basis through a widely used visa pathway.

New and pending applications under the Permanent Labor Certification Program, or PERM, have been frozen. This is a big blow to Indians who hold a majority of H-1B visas - a temporary visa for specialists - which they used to work in the US while relying on PERM to get a green card and, ultimately, citizenship.

The latest announcement is in line with Trump's push for stricter skilled-worker immigration rules, which tech firms have been adapting to and, therefore, the impact on businesses may be minimal, experts say.

Nasscom, the trade association of India's $300bn (£226bn) technology industry, says that Indian companies have reduced the dependence on H-1B visas and are hiring more locally.

"Consequently, the number of employees transitioning from H-1B visas to permanent residency through the PERM process is also relatively limited," the association adds.

Wipro said in a statement that more than 80% of its workforce in the US is locally hired. Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), said its PERM applications were in single digits in the last two years. Microsoft said in a statement that it has filed for H-1B visas mostly to retain existing staff, not to import new workers.

A report in Business Standard newspaper, citing PERM Tracker, said, TCS' applications filings fell to two in 2025-26 from 513 in the previous year and 1,804 in the year before that. The report said no records were found for Infosys and Wipro for 2025-26.

BBC's email to all eight companies asking questions about the impact of the restriction and how they were supporting affected employees in the US remained unanswered.

Brokerage firm HDFC Securities said the impact on tech firms would be minimal, as PERM-linked jobs make up only a small share of revenue, even if higher-paid American workers replace them.

But the US government's decision has an impact beyond business.

A US-based senior executive with one of these eight firms told the BBC on condition of anonymity that the new PERM restriction will "not break the business", but the impact is more "intense" at a human level.

"A good number of people we know are stuck in a space where they have spent some years in the US but their green card application hasn't moved. Even if they are ready to move back to India, their children don't want to because they grew up here," he said.

Recent policy moves have deepened uncertainty and amplified online hostility towards Indian immigrants and H-1B visa holders.

Researchers at Stop AAPI Hate, a US non-profit that combats anti-Asian and Pacific Islander discrimination, have reported a sharp increase in anti-South Asian online sentiment since the 2024 US election, with Indian immigrants and H-1B visa holders being frequent targets.

While barring the eight tech companies from PERM, US Vice President JD Vance too referred to foreign professionals holding H-1B visas as "foreign indentured servants".

While he later acknowledged that it was an "imperfect" rhetoric, his remark drew sharp criticism from India's foreign ministry which called it "unwarranted" and "deeply offensive" for the colonial connotation.

Poorvi Chothani, founder and managing partner of global immigration law firm LawQuest, said many came to the US for better prospects, borrowing heavily to study and build careers. But as rules tighten now, they have fewer options and less ability to absorb the costs.

Immigration experts believe that as pathways for residency become limited, some may reconsider their future in the US, while others may choose not to move at all.

Ahmet Gulek, Postdoctoral Fellow at Stanford's Immigration Policy Lab, told BBC that despite alternate ways to get residency, not many may be feasible.

While moving to another firm not covered by the suspension is an option, he flags that it's unclear if those firms would be open to hiring immigrants given "the fear of retaliation".

The technology industry has already been reshaped by layoffs, cost-cutting and the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), making career moves tougher.

But there are other routes to a US green card. People with exceptional accomplishments or whose work advances national interests may be eligible for categories that bypass the PERM labour certification process.

Applicants can also qualify for permanent residency by investing at least $800,000 in eligible US enterprises.

Gulek warns some of these categories "may be targeted next."

While Chothani says some are so keen to stay in the US that they are considering the EB-5 investor route but may not have enough capital to invest.

Nearly one million Indian nationals were waiting for employment-based green cards as of December 2025, representing 79% of the total pending applications, according to the National Foundation for American Policy (NFAP).

Their report projects wait times ranging from five to 179 years for highly skilled Indians filing labour certification or employment-based immigration petitions from January 2026, depending on the visa category.

Like other recent immigration measures, the PERM suspension may face federal court challenges. But together, these moves signal a more restrictive climate for those hoping to study, work or settle in the US.

Earlier, the Trump administration imposed a $100,000 fee on certain new H-1B visa petitions, a measure that was later struck down by federal courts. More recently, it has also proposed a $70,000 fee for universities recommending international students for a programme that allows graduates to work in the country after completing their studies.

"This trend is not changing anytime soon," said an Indian professional, who spoke to BBC on condition of anonymity and has transitioned to an H-1B visa recently after a "long wait". He says both the Republican Party and the Democratic Party agree immigration laws need reform, even if they disagree on how.

Some research suggests that restrictions could shift jobs to India rather than to American workers. This is supported by industry players saying that they are already witnessing an increase in companies offshoring work.

"Companies benefit from cost arbitrage when they move work offshore. Post Covid, there is also greater acceptance and appreciation for remote work from clients," the executive from the tech firm earlier quoted says.

Experts believe America's appetite for Indian tech talent is unlikely to disappear. What may be changing is how it taps that talent. For Indian professionals, that could mean rewriting the script about building a future in the US.

items.title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?
items.summary: Musk says there's "a lot to be gained" by combining the firms in what would be the biggest merger in history.
items.content:
Elon Musk has spent years building Tesla and SpaceX into a pair of trillion-dollar technology empires. Now, he is considering bringing them together .

Asked on Tuesday whether a merger would be a good idea, Musk was clear: "Yes."

The prospect is more than hypothetical. Musk said special committees have been formed to assess a potential deal, although he stressed that there is no guarantee a merger will happen and that nothing has been agreed.

With Tesla valued at roughly $1.5 trillion (£1.1 trillion) and SpaceX at $2 trillion, a combination of the two companies would mark the largest merger ever.

Any deal would also need shareholder backing. But Musk said he saw "a lot to be gained" in bringing the businesses together.

"In my opinion, 100%. It's just a question of when," says David Nicholson, chief technology advisor at market research firm The Futurum Group.

During Tesla's earnings call on Wednesday, Musk said he had nothing further to add about the prospect of a merger but quipped: "I feel like I'm tap-dancing through a minefield."

Musk said that calling the merger a certainty would be "overstating" things.

Tesla reported a slight drop in third quarter sales which came in at $28.05 billion compared with $28.1 billion at the same time last year.

The unveiling of the Tesla Roadster last week - a futuristic electric car powered by SpaceX rocket thrusters - served as a "symbolic embodiment" hinting at the two Musk companies merging, Nicholson said.

Musk, chief executive of both SpaceX and Tesla, said bringing the firms together would be beneficial given the work each does around chips, artificial intelligence (AI) and other technology projects.

Specifically, the deal would combine Tesla's cars, robots and self-driving technology with SpaceX's rockets, data centres, satellites and telecommunications operations.

The move could be a step towards Musk's mission to build a self-sustaining city on Mars - a vision that has invited sceptics but also plenty of backers.

Over the past year, Musk has moved to consolidate his businesses, with SpaceX acquiring xAI and X, formerly Twitter, before going public this year.

But the merger would ultimately be decided by shareholders, with half of Tesla's needed to back the deal, a threshold even Musk described as "quite a high hurdle".

Musk, as boss of both companies, cannot participate in shareholder discussions.

Even so, Musk, a key shareholder of Tesla, will likely get his way in the next few years, said investment analyst Dan Sheehan from Telos Wealth Advisors.

He believes shareholders will back the deal as the technology the companies develop complement each other, Sheehan said.

But the merger would mean that Tesla shareholders will likely hold a "smaller slice of a much larger and more complex business," he added.

"There's no real precedent for how a public company like Tesla gets priced in this," Sheehan said.

SpaceX shares rose 8% in after hours trading while shares of Tesla climbed by 2%.

Experts told the BBC that Tesla drivers are unlikely to see much drastic change in the near term, even if the two companies combine.

In fact, vehicles seem almost like "an afterthought", overshadowed by the potential to combine the Tesla and SpaceX's tech capabilities, Nicholson said.

Changes are already underway at Tesla. The carmaker said earlier this year that it would prioritise its best-selling Model Y and Model 3, shifting focus away from less popular models .

Tesla also started using a manufacturing plant in California to produce humanoid robots, known as Optimus.

Pairing Tesla's self-driving technology and robotics with SpaceX's AI and satellite network could result in more capable vehicles, Sheehan said.

"The question is how much priority cars get inside a company increasingly driven by AI infrastructure," he added.

The recent Roadster showcase suggests SpaceX technology could be pulled into future Tesla products, which could attract more customers, said Tu Le, the founder of advisory firm Sino Auto Insights.

The Cybertruck-maker faces intense competition from Chinese carmakers like BYD, which overtook Tesla as the world's biggest EV maker in January.

The biggest winner is probably Musk - the world's richest man who also became the world's first trillionaire earlier this year.

The merger would give Musk greater voting control over the combined company than he currently has at Tesla, a factor the special committee assessing the deal would have to consider.

A single company makes it easier for Musk to run his AI strategy the way he wants, Sheehan said.

"The deal itself doesn't add to Musk's wealth, but it concentrates it further in one stock," he said.

However, the merger could attract scrutiny over Musk, already a polarising figure in the US, Nicholson said.

The move could also face more regulatory pressure if Democrats - many of whom have been critical of Musk - win more seats in the US midterm elections next month.

Shareholders have backed Musk's desires before. Last year, Tesla investors approved an unprecedented compensation package for Musk valued around $1tn .

"I honestly don't think Musk will be keeping track of what the merger will do for his wealth," Nicholson said.

The deal also brings Musk closer to what Nicholson says is "his mission in life": colonising Mars.
